title: PNP stands firm vs alleged attempts to disrupt ASEAN Summit 2026
summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Monday vowed to stand firm against alleged repeated attempts by protesters to disrupt the country's hosting of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits.

blocks.text: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Monday vowed to stand firm against alleged repeated attempts by protesters to disrupt the country's hosting of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits.
In a statement, PNP chief Police General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said sufficient police personnel would remain deployed at summit venues.
“Hindi nagkulang ang inyong PNP sa pakiusap at paalala sa ating mga kababayan na ilagay sa tamang lugar at panahon ang pagsasagawa ng protesta,” Nartatez said.
(Your PNP has not failed to ask and remind our countrymen to hold the protest at the right place and time.)
“Hindi po ugali ng mga Pilipino ang mambastos at ilagay sa alanganin ang seguridad ng ating mga bisita,” he said.
(It is not the habit of Filipinos to be rude and jeopardize the security of our guests.)

Nartatez said police commanders had repeatedly appealed to protesters to conduct their activities peacefully and away from summit venues. However, he said police personnel had to enforce the law after protesters supposedly disregarded their appeals and affected public order.
According to the PNP, some protesters allegedly tried to break the police line to hold their activities at the ASEAN Summit venues.

Nartatez said the PNP would continue to observe maximum tolerance and maintain a defensive posture but would not allow any action that could compromise the safety of ASEAN leaders, delegates, visitors, and other guests.
“While we maintain a defensive posture and continue to observe maximum tolerance, we will not allow any action that will compromise the safety of any of our guests,” he added.

He also directed the National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) and other police units to sustain security measures for the remaining summit activities and remain professional in handling succeeding demonstrations.
Meanwhile, Nartatez defended police personnel deployed to manage the protest actions amid allegations against some of them.
“Let us recognize that our personnel on the ground were performing their duties under challenging circumstances, repeatedly appealing to protesters to cooperate and avoid confrontation,” he said.
“We will stand by our men and women who perform their duties professionally and lawfully, but we assure the public that any deviation from our standards is addressed accordingly,” he added.
On Sunday, Nartatez visited a hospital where two PNP personnel deployed for the ASEAN Summit were confined following separate incidents.
One of the officers was reportedly in a coma, while the other was a motorcycle rider who figured in an accident, according to the PNP. —AOL, GMA News
